edits.before: Fatal callbacks use separate disposable children only after a same-lineage actual49-case resource review. A Jco failure must follow a durable post-import/pre-call marker and a complete caught throw, or a bounded SIGABRT after that marker. A writer failure/normal return/preflight failure cannot pass. WT must also carry the source-specific diagnostic; an uninformative generic trap remains inconclusive. Timeout, forced cleanup, or unrelated signals never count as expected fatal. Native abort can prevent worker-finally code; the parent still performs its final audit, without claiming the worker audit ran.
edits.after: Fatal attempts use separate disposable children only after a same-lineage actual49-case resource review. A durable post-import/pre-call marker plus a complete caught throw, or a bounded SIGABRT, records an invocation failure only. Expected-label and unrelated opaque Errors, primitive throws and generic aborts cannot establish the deliberate callback cause. The Jco classification is always cause-inconclusive with expectedCallbackFailureProved/fatalCallbackGateSatisfied false; this family has no genuine current355 callback diagnostic channel. There is no fatal-gate PASS contract. A complete observation publication may finish while that gate remains explicitly unaccepted. Writer failure, normal return, pre-arm/preflight failure, timeout/forced cleanup and unrelated signals refuse even this observation. WT retains the stricter source-specific diagnostic requirement; it does not turn Jco ambiguity into callback proof. Native abort can prevent worker-finally code; only the parent final audit is attempted independently.
